newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Calif., finances given high marks.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Calif., finances given high marks.

text.p: Orange County's outside auditor gave a top rating to the California county's financial statements for the budget year that ended June 30, 1996, a county finance official said on Friday.

The auditing firm Ernst & Young LLP issued an "unqualified" opinion on the county's 1995-96 financial statements, finding that the county's internal controls were adequate and that its transactions were fairly stated, Gary Burton, the county's chief financial officer, said.
"It's another sign of the county's financial recovery," Burton said.
Last year, the county received a "qualified" opinion.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
